title: Phaeromularia fruit and leaf spots of citrus

Header: Phaeromularia fruit and leaf spots of citrus

Prevention: Establish orchards using clean seedlings free from diseases sourced from
Prune the trees to reduce humidity in the orchard as this favors disease development.
Mulch plants to avoid spread of fungi to lower leaves.
Collect old plant debris from the field immediately after harvest and burn to reduce inoculum levels for the next season crop.
Regularly weed the fields to reduce humidity within citrus crops, thus preventing infection.
When establishing the orchard, space the plants at about 6x6m (small varieties) and 8 x 8m (large varieties) to improve aeration.
Monitoring: Look for: greenish yellow spots on leaves which later turn brown with a yellow halo.
Brown sunken circular spots with raised edges and a yellow halo on fruit, giving a blister like appearance.
Dark brown spots on stems, which may merge and cause dieback.
Scout weekly for presence of spots especially during wet weather which favors disease development.
Take action when 30% of leafspots are seen on a plant.
Direct Control: Practice field sanitation by removing and destroying (e.g by burning) infected plant parts/ plant debris to reduce disease inoculum on the farm.
Add 10 ml soap to 1L of water and stir to mix.
Add 50 ml neem oil to the 1L water-soap solution and mix thouroughly.
Add the oil-water- soap solution to 14 litres water in the knapsack and apply within 8 hrs.
Trianum-P ( Trichoderma harzianum ) at a rate of 15g in 5L or
Trichotech ( Trichoderma asperellum ) at a rate of 2.5g in 20L of water.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Apply copper based fungicide such as, Vitra 40 wg, Champflo at 50g/20l of water.
Start spraying when you notice brown spots on the leaves.
Oshothane, Dithane at the rate of 50g/20L of water.
Spray with chlorothalonil based fungicides such as
Compliant 560 (40ml/20L of water); Daconil 720 (85ml/20L of water).
Repeat every 7-14 days for as long as needed.
